sources.title: University of Iowa piano reference recordings
Model-based digital pianos: from physics to sound synthesis
The simulation of piano string vibration: From physical models to finite difference schemes and digital waveguides

provenance.notes: Tuning, inharmonicity, and decay use mf and ff recordings at C2, C3, Gb3, C4, C5, Eb5, C6, A6, and C7. Values between anchors use linear interpolation, and each direct stiffness and loss row includes that key's stretch tuning. Low-bass loss values blend back to the generic model at A0; upper values use the C7 anchor. The three shared felt centers use non-harmonic attack residuals from the same notes. Per-key choir levels, unison width, hammer contact, filter, and felt register terms follow smooth model curves because the recordings do not isolate those parts. The key-to-body-mode matrix is also a smooth modeled bridge projection because the recordings do not isolate soundboard mode shapes. The short bridge, body, FDN, damper, radiation, and sympathetic values stay modeled.
